stages.title: Selecting All Columns
stages.concept: Retrieving all rows and columns using SELECT *
learningObjectives: Construct basic SELECT * FROM table queries
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Selecting All Columns in SQL

To retrieve all columns from a relational database table, use the wildcard asterisk (`*`) operator inside a `SELECT` statement. This projects all fields for matching rows in the specified target table.

```sql
SELECT * FROM users;
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Database Beacon

Write a query to select all columns from the table named `agents`.
stages.outputFormat: Query result table containing all rows from agents

examples.explanation: Retrieves all columns from agents table.

stages.starterCode: -- Write a query to select all columns from agents

testCases.expectedOutput: SELECT * FROM agents;
SELECT * FROM agents;

stages.title: Selecting Specific Columns
stages.concept: Column projection using SELECT col1, col2
prerequisites: Retrieving all rows and columns using SELECT *
learningObjectives: Select specific columns by name to reduce dataset width
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Column Projection in SQL

To retrieve only specific attributes rather than full table rows, list comma-separated column names in your `SELECT` clause. This reduces network payload and improves query execution speed.

```sql
SELECT username, score FROM players;
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Targeted Projection

Write a query to select only the `name` and `rank` columns from the `agents` table.
stages.starterCode: -- Write query to select name and rank from agents

testCases.expectedOutput: SELECT name, rank FROM agents;
SELECT name, rank FROM agents;

stages.title: Filtering Rows with WHERE
stages.concept: Filtering rows using the WHERE clause
prerequisites: Column projection using SELECT col1, col2
learningObjectives: Filter rows using comparison operators in WHERE clause
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Filtering Rows with WHERE

The `WHERE` clause filters dataset rows based on conditional boolean expressions. Only table records evaluating to `TRUE` for the predicate condition are included in the returned output.

```sql
SELECT * FROM users WHERE total_xp >= 1000;
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Signal Filter

Write a query to select all columns from `agents` where `status` is equal to `'active'`.
stages.starterCode: -- Write query to select active agents

testCases.expectedOutput: SELECT * FROM agents WHERE status = 'active';
SELECT * FROM agents WHERE status = 'active';

stages.title: Logical Operators in WHERE
stages.concept: Combining criteria using AND / OR in WHERE clause
prerequisites: Filtering rows using the WHERE clause
learningObjectives: Combine multiple boolean predicates using AND and OR
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Compound Conditions in WHERE

Combine multiple filtering criteria in SQL using logical `AND` and `OR` operators. `AND` requires both condition predicates to be true, while `OR` requires at least one predicate to be true.

```sql
SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'gear' AND price < 50;
```

stages.title: Sorting Results
stages.concept: Ordering query results using ORDER BY ASC/DESC
prerequisites: Filtering rows using the WHERE clause
learningObjectives: Sort results in ascending or descending order
stages.lessonContentMd:
## ORDER BY Clause in SQL

Sort returned query records using the `ORDER BY` clause. Specify `ASC` for ascending order (default) or `DESC` for descending order based on one or more column values.

```sql
SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY total_xp DESC;
```

stages.title: Limiting Output
stages.concept: Limiting result set count using LIMIT
prerequisites: Ordering query results using ORDER BY ASC/DESC
learningObjectives: Cap the number of returned rows using LIMIT
stages.lessonContentMd:
## LIMIT Clause in SQL

The `LIMIT` clause caps the maximum number of rows returned by a query. When combined with `ORDER BY`, it enables fetching top-N leaderboard records or pagination subsets.

```sql
SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY total_xp DESC LIMIT 5;
```
stages.problemStatementMd:

stages.title: Counting Rows
stages.concept: Counting total rows using aggregate COUNT(*)
prerequisites: Retrieving all rows and columns using SELECT *
learningObjectives: Calculate row count using aggregate function COUNT(*)
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Aggregate Function: COUNT(*)

The `COUNT(*)` aggregate function returns the total number of rows matching your query criteria, including rows with NULL values in individual columns.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agents;
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Roster Census

Write a query to count the total number of rows in the `agents` table.
stages.starterCode: -- Write query to count total rows in agents

testCases.expectedOutput: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agents;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agents;

stages.title: Sum & Average
stages.concept: Numeric aggregations with SUM() and AVG()
prerequisites: Calculate row count using aggregate function COUNT(*)
learningObjectives: Calculate numeric totals using SUM() and averages using AVG()
stages.lessonContentMd:
## Numeric Aggregations: SUM and AVG

SQL provides built-in functions to compute summary mathematical metrics across numerical table columns:
- `SUM(column)` returns total added sum
- `AVG(column)` calculates average value

```sql
SELECT SUM(xp_earned), AVG(xp_earned) FROM daily_activity;
```
stages.problemStatementMd:
## Resource Total

Write a query to calculate the `SUM(total_xp)` from the `users` table.
stages.starterCode: -- Write query to calculate sum of total_xp from users

testCases.expectedOutput: SELECT SUM(total_xp) FROM users;
SELECT SUM(total_xp) FROM users;

stages.title: Group By Aggregations
stages.concept: Grouping row metrics using GROUP BY
prerequisites: Calculate row count using aggregate function COUNT(*)
learningObjectives: Group aggregate metrics per category using GROUP BY
stages.lessonContentMd:
## GROUP BY Clause in SQL

The `GROUP BY` clause groups rows sharing common attribute values so aggregate functions (`COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`) compute separate metrics per category group.

```sql
SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM tools GROUP BY category;
```
stages.problemStatementMd:

examples.output: SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM tools GROUP BY category;

stages.starterCode: -- Write query to group tools by category
stages.solutionCode: SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM tools GROUP BY category;

testCases.expectedOutput: SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM tools GROUP BY category;
SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM tools GROUP BY category;

stages.title: Inner Table Joins
stages.concept: Combining rows from multiple tables using INNER JOIN
prerequisites: Group aggregate metrics per category using GROUP BY
learningObjectives: Combine related table records using INNER JOIN ... ON
stages.lessonContentMd:
## INNER JOIN in SQL

`INNER JOIN` combines related rows from two or more tables based on a foreign key relationship predicate specified in the `ON` clause.

```sql
SELECT users.username, user_tools.progress_pct
FROM users
INNER JOIN user_tools ON users.id = user_tools.user_id;
```
stages.problemStatementMd:

stages.starterCode: -- Write inner join query between stages and tools
stages.solutionCode: SELECT stages.title, tools.name FROM stages INNER JOIN tools ON stages.tool_id = tools.id;

testCases.expectedOutput: SELECT stages.title, tools.name FROM stages INNER JOIN tools ON stages.tool_id = tools.id;
